text.flavor: While the road waits, the Host takes up the work at hand: hauling, mending, tending, building, and drilling for what comes next.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and Choose 1:
  • Gain 2 Coins
  • Gain 1 Coin and 1 Leadership
  • Repair 1 damaged Baggage Train space: Spend 1 Wood.

If you have the Camp Steward, you may instead Advance 2 Time and Choose 1:
  • Gain 1 Resource matching the adjacent Terrain
  • Buy 1 resource from the Market for 1 Coin less than its current Buy value.

CAMP-002.title: Market Day

text.flavor: The market rarely favors the impatient, but it often rewards the watchful.
text.effect:
If you have constructed a Market, you may also perform this at any Controlled Settlement.

Advance 1 Time. Buy and/or Sell up to 2 Resources at Market value. Subject to Baggage Train capacity.

CAMP-002.notes: Keyword normalized to Civic from the card icon; legacy Keyword_text says Field.

text.flavor: Stone and timber raise the walls, but belief and learning decide what kind of place stands within them.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and Choose 1:
  • Chapel: Cost: 1 Wood and 1 Coin. Gain Priest.
  • Academy: Cost: 1 Stone and 1 Coin

Place the matching token on your Player Board.

text.flavor: The frontier yields little to those who only pass through. It rewards the ones who leave something behind.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and Choose 1:
  • Market: Cost: 1 Wood and 1 Coin.
  • Baggage Cart: Cost: 1 Wood

Place the matching token on your Player Board.

text.flavor: Silver spent on quiet study often returns in louder ways.
text.effect: Advance 2 Time, Spend 1 Coin and Gain 1 Research token.

text.flavor: There are always swords for hire where fear is near and silver is honest.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time Recruit up to 3 Mercenaries (Infantry class) for 1 Coin each.

Mercenaries:
  • May exceed Host MU limits
  • Use white Mercenary tokens.
  • Disband from your Host in the Winter season.

text.flavor: Coin opens storehouses that pride or haste would leave closed.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time, Spend 3 Coins and Choose one:
  • Gain 1 Food and 1 Wood.
  • Gain 1 Food and 1 Stone.
  • Gain 1 Wood and 1 Stone.

Subject to Baggage Train capacity.

text.flavor: The march pauses long enough for weariness to loosen its grip.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time, Spend 1 Leadership and 1 Food.

Gain 2 Leadership and 1 Morale.

CAMP-009.title: Raise Local Levies

text.flavor: Not every man who joins the host seeks glory. Some answer because the road has reached their door.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time, Spend 1 Leadership and 1 Food.

Add 2 Levy into your Host.

CAMP-009.notes: Cost normalized from Effect text: 1 Leadership + 1 Food; legacy Cost field lists only 1F.

text.flavor: A host that trains in earnest soon learns what kind of war it means to fight.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time, Spend 1 Leadership.

Choose 1:
  • You may immediately purchase either the top card of the Advancement deck or 1 Armor Development from the R&R Offer. It costs 1 less Research Token, to a minimum of 1. You must still pay all other printed costs.
  • Gain 1 Research. You may discard the top Tactics card for free and reveal the next one, though you may not purchase it during this phase.

text.flavor: A gift sent ahead may cool a grudge that steel would only sharpen.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and Choose 1 Hostile tribe and pay its Tribute below, then Roll 2d6. The normal Hostile -1 DRM does not apply to this roll. On 8+: gain 1 Rapport with that tribe.

Tribute:
  • Sun-Touched: 1 Stone
  • Nightstone Clan: 1 Food
  • The Quietus: 1 Wood
  • Pale Hands: 1 of your highest-value resource. If multiple resources are tied for highest value, choose one of them.

text.flavor: A wise commander does not march on courage alone. Scouts find the road, and Stewards keep the Host ready to follow it.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and Choose 1:
Train Scouts: Cost: 1 Research. Place the Scouting token near the Explore draw deck.

Appoint Camp Steward: Cost: 2 Coin. Place the Camp Steward token near the Camp draw deck.

text.flavor: Bread shared in peace can carry a promise farther than a threat ever will.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time, Spend 1 Food.

Choose a Neutral or Friendly tribe and test 8+, appling any Rapport DRM.
  • Pass: Gain 2 Coins and 1 Rapport with that tribe. If the chosen tribe is already Friendly, gain 1 Morale instead.
  • Fail: Gain 1 Coin.

text.flavor: The mugs keep coming, the dice keep rolling, and good judgment is first out the door.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time. You may pay 1 coin to Roll 1d6. You may not use Leadership to alter your result:
1: Lose 1 Morale. Your host shakes their head in disapproval.
2: Leave the tavern with your reputation intact.
3: Gain 1 Coin.
4: Gain 1 Coin and 1 Leadership. You may pay 1 Coin to try again.
5: Gain 2 Coins and 1 Leadership. You may pay 1 Coin to try again.
6: Gain 3 Coins, 1 Leadership. You may pay 1 Coin to try again.

text.flavor: The market square is loud with petty disputes, rigged contests, and one prize goat that has somehow become a matter of honor.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Roll 1d6:
1: You misjudge the mood. Lose 1 Leadership.
2: No one is satisfied. No effect.
3: Gain 1 Coin.
4: Gain 1 Leadership.
5: Gain 1 Morale and 1 Coin.
6:Gain 1 Leadership and 1 Morale.

text.flavor: Before the gathered faithful, your victory was an insult that could not be ignored. The fire has not forgotten. It comes now to burn shame away in battle.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and discard all drawn Camp cards except the Work card. If The Sun-Touched are no longer Hostile, return this card to the unseeded Echo Supply.

If The Sun-Touched are Hostile: You may Parley: Pay 2 resources matching the terrain adjacent to this Settlement or pay 5 Coin. Then test Rapport (9+). Do not apply the Hostile Rapport DRM to this test.

• Pass: Set this tribe to Neutral and return this card to the unseeded Echoes pile.
• Fail, Cannot Pay, or Decline to Parley: The tribe attacks.

After resolving this Echo, end the Camp Phase.


Enemy Host
Year 1: 2A, 2I, 1L
Year 2: 3A, 2I, 2L
Year 3: 2A, 1C, 2I, 3L

text.flavor: They do not howl for vengeance. They come in silence, pale faces streaked with ash, to reclaim what was taken and punish the hand that dared to hold it.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and discard all drawn Camp cards except the Work card. If The Pale Hands are no longer Hostile, return this card to the unseeded Echo Supply.

If The Pale Hands are Hostile: You may Parley: Pay 2 resources matching the terrain adjacent to this Settlement, or pay 5 Coin. Then test Rapport (9). Do not apply the Hostile Rapport DRM to this test.

• Pass: Set this tribe to Neutral and return this card to the unseeded Echoes pile.
• Fail, Cannot Pay, or Decline to Parley: The tribe attacks.

After resolving this Echo, end the Camp Phase.


Enemy Host
Year 1: 3I, 2L
Year 2: 1A, 3I, 3L
Year 3: 1A, 4I, 3L

text.flavor: The Nightstone Clan does not forgive defeat. They watch, they wait, and when you grow comfortable behind your own walls, they strike with cold purpose.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and discard all drawn Camp cards except the Work card. If The Nightstone Clan are no longer Hostile, return this card to the unseeded Echo Supply.

If The Nightstone Clan are Hostile: You may Parley: Pay 2 resources matching the terrain adjacent to this Settlement, or pay 5 Coin. Then test Rapport (9). Do not apply the Hostile Rapport DRM to this test.

• Pass: Set this tribe to Neutral and return this card to the unseeded Echoes pile.
• Fail, Cannot Pay, or Decline to Parley: The tribe attacks.

After resolving this Echo, end the Camp Phase.


Enemy Host
Year 1: 2A, 1C, 2I
Year 2: 1A, 1C, 2I, 2L
Year 3: 2A, 1C, 2I, 3L

text.flavor: No oath was shouted. No challenge was given. Yet the trespass lingers like a stain. When the Quietus comes, it does so with the certainty of a sentence already passed.
text.effect:
Advance 2 Time and discard all drawn Camp cards except the Work card. If The Quietus are no longer Hostile, return this card to the unseeded Echo Supply.

If The Quietus are Hostile: You may Parley: Pay 2 resources matching the terrain adjacent to this Settlement, or pay 5 Coin. Then test Rapport (9). Do not apply the Hostile Rapport DRM to this test.

• Pass: Set this tribe to Neutral and return this card to the unseeded Echoes pile.
• Fail, Cannot Pay, or Decline to Parley: The tribe attacks.

After resolving this Echo, end the Camp Phase.


Enemy Host
Year 1: 1P, 1A, 1I, 2L
Year 2: 1P, 1A, 1I, 5L
Year 3: 1P, 1A, 2I, 6L

text.flavor: A child’s careless game has set dry kindling smoldering near a granary. The danger is small now. It will not stay that way for long.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Roll 2d6:
8+: The fire is put out in time for grateful eyes to see it. Gain 1 Morale. Seed 1 random Q Echo.

7 or less: The flame is stamped out before anyone even notices. No effect.

text.flavor: The child’s little blaze never reached the granary, and the people nearby know why. News of your host’s quick action has traveled ahead of the march to places where full storehouses still matter.
text.effect:
Gain 1 Food, 1 Wood, and 1 Morale.

Those who heard the tale offer provisions freely, grateful that your host once kept smoke from becoming ruin.

ECHO-Q-02.title: The Child Still Tells the Story

text.flavor: The child whose game set the kindling smoking still tells how your host stepped in before the flames could spread to the granary. The tale has moved ahead of your march, and strangers now look on your host more favorably than they otherwise would.
text.effect:
Gain 1 Morale and 1 Leadership.

People receive your host more warmly, and that goodwill lends extra weight to your words.

text.flavor: The child’s little blaze that threatened the granary did not begin as carelessly as it seemed. Now, the one who meant the granary to burn finds your host and makes their displeasure known.
text.effect:
Roll 1d6:
1-2: Lose 1 Leadership. They catch your host off guard and muddy the truth before witnesses.

3-4: No effect. The accusation comes to nothing, but leaves a sour taste.

5-6: Gain 1 Leadership. Your host turns the confrontation back on them and comes away looking sharper.

text.flavor: There is shouting at Pepperridge Farm that draws your host’s attention. Dr. Pepper, known nearby for treating sick horses and troubled cattle, and his family are being harassed by the Crumb family, a local rival bakery, who accuse them of stealing recipes. The Crumbs offer food and silver for your backing, though your host can see well enough that both were taken from the Pepper family’s own stores.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time. You may side with the Crumb family.

If you do, gain 2 Food and 5 Coin. Seed 1 random P Echo.

text.flavor: Your host did not leave Pepperridge Farm that day as rich as it had hoped. Dr. Pepper took solace in knowing that the food taken from his family’s stores would do your host no good. A man who knows beasts and sickness also knows what spoiled stores can do to a marching army.
text.effect:
Lose 1 Infantry and 2 Levy.

The food taken that day turned foul in camp, and the sickness that followed is no accident. Dr. Pepper was heard boasting, “The joke’s on them. They’ll need that silver to hire and train more troops.”

text.flavor: Your host did not leave Pepperridge Farm that day as unnoticed as it had hoped. The silver taken from that quarrel is long spent, but the insult has only grown in the telling.
text.effect:
Now Dr. Pepper has caught up with your march, backed by furious kin, flour-dusted bakers, and enough hard-handed farm folk to make good on his grievance at last.

Advance 1 Time and Fight a Combat against Dr. Pepper’s Host, consisting of 2A, 1C, 3I and 4L. You may not disengage from this combat. If you lose, you are defeated by Dr. Pepper. From Pepperridge Farm. Because you stuck your nose into a dispute over baked goods and your campaign ends.

text.flavor: Your host did not leave Pepperridge Farm that day as quietly as it had hoped. Dr. Pepper has seen to it that the story spread ahead of your march, and always in the same telling: your host took stolen food and silver because greed came easier than judgment.
text.effect:
The tale has done its work. You have been arrested and face justice from the local law.

Advance 1 Time. Lose 5 Coin and 1 Morale.

If you cannot pay the full 5 Coin, lose all Coin you have and spend the next week in the town gaol. Advance the calendar 1 additional space for time served.

The silver is seized, the fine is paid, and your host leaves with a new name in local gossip: the Baked Good Bandits.

text.flavor: A family’s cart has broken an axle in the mud, and much of their life lies scattered in the road around them. Others have passed them by. Your host can stop, lend hands, and set the cart right before the road swallows the day entire.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Roll 2d6:
6+: The cart is righted, the axle bound well enough to travel, and the family parts from your host with gratitude plain on every face. Gain 1 Morale. Seed 1 random C Echo.

5 or less: The cart is righted all the same, but the help is taken more as necessity than kindness. No effect.

text.flavor: The family whose cart your host helped right did not remain unlucky for long. A letter reached them not many weeks later bearing news of a previously unknown kinsman and an inheritance they had never expected to see. Remembering who stopped in the mud when others rode on, they have sought your host out to repay the kindness in full.
text.effect:
Gain 2 Food, 4 Coin, and 1 Morale.

They press good stores and honest silver into your hands, grateful that someone chose to help when they had little left to offer in return.

ECHO-C-02.title: The Road Was Spoken Well Of

text.flavor: The family whose cart your host helped right had no silver windfall to share, but neither did they let the kindness vanish into the mud. They spoke of your host wherever the road carried them, and the tale has gone ahead of your march in quieter ways than coin.
text.effect:
Gain 1 Food, 1 Morale, and 1 Leadership.

People receive your host with a little more warmth, and that goodwill lends extra weight to your words.

text.flavor: The family whose cart your host helped right had little to spare when first you met them, and little more for some time after. But the road has crossed your paths again, and they have not forgotten who stopped in the mud when others passed them by.
text.effect:
Gain 1 Coin.

It is not much, but this time they insist on paying something for the help they once could not repay.

text.flavor: A roadside shrine has become a place of local giving. Candles burn low, coins sit in the offering bowl, and food for the poor rests under cloth beside the stone.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time. When your host stops nearby, a sudden uproar breaks out: silver is missing, and one of your men is being named as the thief. The charge cannot be proven, but your host can feel how badly the locals want someone to answer for it.

You leave the matter unsettled and march on rather than lose time to finding the truth. Seed 1 random M Echo.

text.flavor: The silver missing from the shrine was not misplaced after all. Word has caught up with your host that the accused man truly did take it, and now the locals mean to see the matter answered. The culprit is handed over to the law, and your host must make what restitution it can besides.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Remove 1 unit from your Host in this order: Cavalry, then Infantry, then Archer, then Levy. Then roll 1d3 and pay that much Coin in restitution.

If you cannot pay the full amount, pay all Coin you have and lose 1 Morale. The truth is known at last, and the host is left to swallow what dignity it can.

text.flavor: The silver missing from the shrine was taken, but not by the man named under your banner. The true thief has been found, and the accusation that followed your host falls away at last.
text.effect:
Gain 1 Morale.

The man’s name is cleared, and the relief runs through the host faster than the rumor ever did.

text.flavor: A muddy ring forms at the edge of camp. Coins flash, voices rise, and the Host looks to you: will one of your own step forward?
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Choose one:

• Send in a Fighter: Choose 1 Military Unit in your Host and roll 1d6:
1: Lose that Unit. Seed 1 random B Echo.
2-3: Lose 1 Morale. Seed 1 random B Echo.
4-5: Gain 2 Coins. Seed 1 random D Echo.
6: Gain 3 Coins and 1 Morale. Seed 1 random D Echo.

• Refuse the Challenge: Lose 1 Morale.

text.flavor: The victory has become a campfire legend, retold louder with every passing night.
text.effect: Gain 1 Morale.

text.flavor: Your champion’s name travels ahead of the Host, drawing cheers, wagers, and eager hangers-on.
text.effect:
Gain 1 Leadership.

You may recruit 1 Levy for free.

text.flavor: The Host has not forgotten the wager, nor the cost paid in the ring.
text.effect:
Test 8+:

Pass: No effect.

Fail: Lose 1 Leadership and 1 Morale.

text.flavor: The beaten fighter’s kin have carried the insult farther than the road should allow.
text.effect:
Test 7+:

Pass: The matter settles.

Fail: Lose 1 Morale.

SCENE-021.title: The Pig That Became a Lord

text.flavor: At a neighboring village fair, a fat prize pig escapes its pen, charges through a council moot, knocks over a local banner, and settles proudly into the Lord’s chair. The locals begin arguing whether this is an omen, a joke, or treason. You make a jape about how much the pig resembles the Lord.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Refer to your Rapport with the tribe in or closest to your Host’s location.
  • Friendly or Allied: Seed 1 random E Echo.
  • Neutral or Hostile: Seed 1 random F Echo.

text.flavor: Word of the jape spreads faster than your Host. By the time the tale catches up with you, the Lord himself has claimed the pig as a lucky fool and your jest as proof of good humor.
text.effect: Gain 1 Leadership.

text.flavor: Camp followers, traders, and road-wardens repeat the story with laughter rather than malice. For a few days, your Host is remembered as clever company instead of another column of armed strangers.
text.effect: Gain 1 Coin or 1 Food.

text.flavor: The tale reaches camp in a sharper form than you told it. In the retelling, your jape sounds less like wit and more like contempt for local authority.
text.effect: Lose 1 Leadership.

text.flavor: A small party of offended retainers reaches your camp carrying the insult in full ceremonial outrage. They insist the story has made their lord a laughingstock across the road.
text.effect: Lose 1 Morale.

text.flavor: A village keeps firepots, pitch jars, and old siege oil for defense. The stores are dangerous, poorly sealed, and exactly the sort of thing that could break an enemy line if used first.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Choose 1:
  • Take the Firepots: Place the Firepots token in your Baggage Train. Seed one random U Echo.
  • Condemn the Stockpile: Gain +1 Leadership. Lose 1 Morale.

Firepots effect: Before the first round of a Combat you may discard it to roll 3d6. For each 4+ rolled, assign 1 casualty to the enemy Host. Assign casualties as if it were a Cavalry attack.

text.flavor: The jars were never meant to travel. One cracks in the night, and the Baggage Train wakes to smoke, shouting, and burning straw.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time. If the Firepots token is still in your Baggage Train, Test 9+.

  • Pass: Discard this Echo. Leave the Firepots token in its Baggage Train slot.
  • Fail: BANG! BANG! Remove the Firepots token. Damage its Baggage Train slot and 1 adjacent Baggage Train slot of your choice. If the adjacent slot contains a Resource, lose that Resource. Remove this Echo from the game.

If the Firepots token is no longer in your Baggage Train, Remove this card.

text.flavor: The pitch seeps through its wrappings. The stink spreads through the carts, clings to blankets, fouls food, and makes every soldier nervous about striking sparks.
text.effect:
If the Firepots token is still in your Baggage Train, Advance 1 Time and Choose 1:
  • Dump the Firepots: Remove the Firepots token from your Baggage Train and Remove this Echo from the game.
  • Carry the Risk: Remove this card from the game and Seed the remaining U Echo into the Camp discard pile.

If the Firepots token is no longer in your Baggage Train, Remove this card.

text.flavor: A battlefield surgeon offers the Host a bitter black draught used by mercenaries who need men standing longer than men should. He does not call it medicine. He calls it time bought in advance.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Choose 1:
  • Take the Draught: Gain the Painkiller token. Seed the K Echo.
  • Refuse the Dose: Gain +1 Morale.

Painkiller effect: Whenever you would lose 1 or more Military Units or Levy from any game effect, including Combat, roll 1d6 for each unit that would be lost. On 5–6, prevent that unit loss. On 1–4, lose that unit normally. This benefit remains active until removed.

text.flavor: The draught still works. That may be the worst thing about it.
text.effect:
Test 8+.

  • Pass: Discard this Echo. Keep the Painkiller token.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Morale, then Remove the Painkiller token and this Echo.

text.flavor: The officers find a marching cadence that keeps the Host moving long after common sense says to stop. Boots strike road. Wagons creak. No one complains because no one has breath left to complain.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Choose 1:
  • Force the March: Gain the Forced March token. Gain +1 Morale and 1 Leadership. Seed one random L Echo.
  • Keep a Human Pace: No effect.

Forced March effect: While this token is active, your Explore phase costs 1 Time instead of 2 Time.

text.flavor: The rhythm is breaking. Men stumble, curses spread, and the road begins taking payment in flesh and patience.
text.effect:
Test 7+.

  • Pass: Choose 1:
    • Keep the Cadence: Lose 1 Leadership. Discard this Echo. Keep the Forced March token.
    • Call a Halt: Advance 2 Time. Remove the Forced March token. Remove this Echo from the game.
  • Fail: Remove the Forced March token. Lose 1 Leadership. Remove this Echo from the game.

text.flavor: The cadence holds. The Host moves faster than it should, farther than it wants, and harder than any road has a right to demand.
text.effect:
Choose 1:
  • Spend Discipline: Lose 1 Leadership. Discard this Echo. Keep the Forced March token.
  • Let Them Breathe: Remove the Forced March token. Gain 1 Morale. Remove this Echo from the game.

text.flavor: The Host tries to forget what it accepted, but the story has already learned to march.
text.effect:
If the Reign in Blood token is active, Test 7+.
  • Pass: Remove the Reign in Blood token. Remove this Echo from the game.
  • Fail: Discard this Echo. The Reign in Blood token remains active.

If the Reign in Blood token is not active, remove this Echo from the game.

text.flavor: Men who once looked away now speak more easily of what must be done. The road has taught them a lesson, and they have learned it too well.
text.effect:
If the Reign in Blood token is active, Lose 1 Morale, then Test 8+.
  • Pass: Remove the Reign in Blood token. Remove this Echo from the game. Gain 1 Morale.
  • Fail: Discard this Echo. The Reign in Blood token remains active.

text.flavor: Word reaches the Host that the dead were found buried, named where possible, and left with enough dignity that strangers stopped to notice.
text.effect: Gain 1 Morale.

text.flavor: Someone who later came upon the graves found more than bodies. The careful burial preserved a sign, seal, or scrap of truth that would have been lost to mud and scavengers.
text.effect: Look at the top 2 cards of the Camp deck. Discard any number of them and return the rest to the top of the deck in any order.

text.flavor: A broad-shouldered local called Big ’Orra strides into camp, points at your banner, and unleashes a speech no one understands. It sounds important. Possibly friendly. Possibly murderous. You answer with equivalent gibberish. This may have been unwise.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Roll 1d6.
  1. ’Orra goes red with fury and lands a big, meaty fist in your face. Lose 1 Morale.
  2. ’Orra spits and gestures sharply. You appear to owe him something. Lose 1 Coin.
  3. No one understands anyone. No Effect.
  4. ’Orra nods as if a serious matter has been settled. Gain 1 Leadership.
  5. ’Orra roars with laughter and claps you on the shoulder. Gain 1 Coin and 1 Leadership.
  6. ’Orra declares you a person of rare wisdom. Apparently. Gain 2 Coin and 1 Morale.

text.flavor: A local priest leads an unfamiliar rite just beyond camp. The drums, chants, and strange gestures unsettle the Host. Soon your soldiers are watching more than resting.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Choose 1:
  • Let the Rite Continue: Advance 1 Time. Seed one random G Echo.
  • Interrupt the Priest: Gain 1 Leadership. Seed one random H Echo.
  • Let Your Priest Judge It: Requirement: Priest. Test 8+.
    • Pass: Gain 1 Leadership and 1 Morale. Seed one random G Echo.
    • Fail: Lose 1 Morale. Seed one random H Echo.

text.flavor: The rite did not end when your Host moved on. It changed. The local priest now tells the story as one of renewal, claiming your presence forced old words to find new meaning.
text.effect: Gain 1 Morale.

text.flavor: A written complaint reaches camp, sealed and formal. The charge is religious, specific, and aimed squarely at your Host.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time and Choose 1:
  • Answer the Charge Lose 1 Leadership. Remove this Echo from the game.
  • Make Restitution: Pay 2 Coin. Remove this Echo from the game.
  • Let Doctrine Speak: Requirement: Priest. Test 7+:
    • Pass: Remove this Echo from the game.
    • Fail: Lose 1 Morale. Remove this Echo from the game.

text.flavor: A violent storm breaks over the Host. By morning, locals say the sky opened because your Host disturbed what it did not understand.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time, Lose 1 Morale.

If you have a Priest, you may Test 8+.
  • Pass: Do not lose the Morale.

ECHO-H-02.title: Falling Off the Edge of the World

text.flavor: Since the rite was disturbed, the road has felt less certain. Guides contradict themselves. Landmarks seem to lose meaning. Even your camp staff begin to doubt their maps.
text.effect:
Advance 1 Time

If you have the Scouting token and/or the Camp Steward token, choose 1 of those tokens and remove it from the game.

If you do not have either token, lose 1 Morale.

ECHO-T-01.title: Sacred Heart

text.flavor: The old stones are remembered by those who still hold your Host close. What was found beneath the trees has become a sign that the road between you has not yet broken.
text.effect:
Check your current Rapport with The Quietus.

If The Quietus are still Allied: Gain 1 Morale or 1 Leadership.

If The Quietus are no longer Allied: Test 7+.
  • Pass: No effect.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Morale.

ECHO-T-01.notes: Legacy camp-cards identifier T1–T4 normalized to EchoPool T + EchoNum.

ECHO-T-02.title: Believer

text.flavor: The Sabbath Stones marked more than old prayer. They marked expectation. The Quietus remember whether your Host treated that expectation as a beginning, a promise, or a thing left behind.
text.effect:
Check your current Rapport with The Quietus.

If The Quietus are now Allied: Test 7+.
  • Pass: Gain 1 Morale or 1 Leadership.
  • Fail: No effect.
  • If The Quietus are still Friendly: Lose 1 Leadership.

If The Quietus are now Neutral or Hostile: Test 7+.
  • Pass: No effect.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Morale.

ECHO-T-02.notes: Legacy camp-cards identifier T1–T4 normalized to EchoPool T + EchoNum.

ECHO-T-03.title: Last in Line

text.flavor: The stones offered no easy meaning when first you found them. Perhaps they were warning. Perhaps invitation. The Quietus now judge what your Host made of the space between you.
text.effect:
Check your current Rapport with The Quietus.

If The Quietus are now Friendly or Allied: Test 7+.
  • Pass: Gain 1 Morale or 1 Leadership.
  • Fail: No effect.

If The Quietus are still Neutral: Lose 1 Leadership.

If The Quietus are now Hostile: Test 7+.
  • Pass: No effect.
  • Fail: Lose 1 Morale.

ECHO-T-03.notes: Legacy camp-cards identifier T1–T4 normalized to EchoPool T + EchoNum.

ECHO-T-04.title: Shot in the Dark

text.flavor: The Sabbath Stones were found while the Quietus stood against you. If there was a lesson in that ring of old marks, it was not freely given. Now the road asks whether anything changed.
text.effect:
Check your current Rapport with The Quietus.

If The Quietus are now Neutral, Friendly, or Allied: Test 7+.
  • Pass: Gain 1 Morale or 1 Leadership.
  • Fail: No effect.

If The Quietus are still Hostile: Lose 1 Morale.

text.effect: Lose 1 Food. If you have the Camp Steward, Test (7) to avoid Food loss.

text.flavor: Massive herds of bison or cattle move across the plains, drawing the attention of local nomads.
text.effect: Gain 1 Food.
